title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The student (EE1) shares their personal identity information (student id) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) during the login and submission process. This act of sharing causes a threat because the portal can identify the student uniquely.

title: Course and Work File Disclosure
description: The student (EE1) shares specific course and work file information (course, work file) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1). This act of sharing causes a threat because the portal can identify the specific academic context and content of the submission.

title: Data Processing and Storage Threat
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the student's data and processes it in a way that causes a threat. The portal may store or process the student's data in a manner that compromises privacy, such as by aggregating data across multiple students or storing it in a way that allows for future identification.

title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The portal exposes the student's unique identifier (student id) in the request payload to the assignment & grading service without any authentication or authorization check. This allows the service to potentially identify the specific student and associate their data with the course.
assumptions: The portal assumes the student id is a public identifier and that the service will not perform any validation.

title: Course Information Leakage
description: The portal sends the course name or ID in the request payload. While this might be necessary for routing, it could be used to identify the specific course context, potentially allowing the service to infer sensitive data about the student's academic standing or history.
assumptions: The portal assumes the course identifier is a standard, non-sensitive field.

title: File Reference Exposure
description: The portal sends the file reference (e.g., filename, path, or hash) in the request payload. This could allow the service to identify the specific file being graded, potentially exposing sensitive information about the student's work or the course content.
assumptions: The portal assumes the file reference is a standard, non-sensitive field.

title: Request Metadata Leakage
description: The portal sends meta-data about the requesting role (e.g., 'student', 'teacher', 'admin') in the request payload. This metadata could be used to link the request to the specific user performing the action, potentially enabling profile-based attacks or targeted data access.
assumptions: The portal assumes the requesting role is a standard, non-sensitive field.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The assignment & grading service receives the student id and course information. Without proper authorization checks, the service may process or store this data in a way that allows it to identify the specific student and associate their data with the course, potentially violating privacy policies.
assumptions: The service assumes the data is necessary for grading and does not perform any additional validation.

title: Assignment File Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares the assignment file with the Assignment Store (DS1) without verifying the recipient's identity or authorization. This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is exposed to an entity that may not be intended to receive it.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The destination element (DataStore DS1) receives the assignment file and stores it in a way that causes a privacy threat. The store may process or store the data without proper access controls, potentially exposing student information to unauthorized parties.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The teacher (EE3) shares their identity information with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) during the login process. This allows the portal to potentially identify the teacher and associate their data with their specific courses.
assumptions: The login process requires the teacher to authenticate and provide their credentials.

title: Data Processing for Identification
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the teacher's identity data and uses it to identify the teacher and associate their data with their specific courses for processing.
assumptions: The portal processes the submitted data to retrieve course information.

title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The portal shares student names and work content with the teacher, which may allow the teacher to identify specific students and access their private work.
assumptions: The teacher has access to the portal and the data is not encrypted or pseudonymized.

title: Student Work Content Exposure
description: The portal shares student work content with the teacher, which may allow the teacher to access private or sensitive information.
assumptions: The teacher has access to the portal and the data is not encrypted or pseudonymized.

title: Teacher Identity Disclosure
description: The teacher (EE3) shares their identity (name, email, or other identifiers) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) when recording a grade. This allows the portal to potentially link or identify the teacher, which may be sensitive information.

title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The teacher (EE3) shares the student's ID with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) when recording a grade. This allows the portal to potentially identify the specific student, which may be sensitive information.

title: Feedback Text Disclosure
description: The teacher (EE3) shares the written feedback text with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) when recording a grade. This allows the portal to potentially store or use the feedback text, which may be sensitive information.

title: Teacher Identity Processing
description: Upon receiving the teacher's identity (EE3) from the source, the Grades Portal Web App (P1) processes or stores this data. If the portal is not configured to anonymize or mask this data, the identity remains accessible.

title: Student Identity Processing
description: Upon receiving the student's ID from the source, the Grades Portal Web App (P1) processes or stores this data. If the portal is not configured to anonymize or mask this data, the identity remains accessible.

title: Feedback Text Processing
description: Upon receiving the feedback text from the source, the Grades Portal Web App (P1) processes or stores this data. If the portal is not configured to anonymize or mask this data, the text remains accessible.

title: Student Identification
description: The source element (P2) shares the student id with the destination (DS2). This act of sharing causes a threat because the recipient (DS2) can identify the specific student receiving the grade record.
assumptions: The student id is unique and known to the source.

title: Course Identification
description: The source element (P2) shares the course information with the destination (DS2). This act of sharing causes a threat because the recipient (DS2) can identify the specific course associated with the grade record.
assumptions: The course information is known to the source.

title: Grader Identification
description: The source element (P2) shares the grader id with the destination (DS2). This act of sharing causes a threat because the recipient (DS2) can identify the specific grader responsible for the grade.
assumptions: The grader id is known to the source.

title: Timestamp Sharing
description: The source element (P2) shares the timestamp with the destination (DS2). This act of sharing causes a threat because the recipient (DS2) can identify the specific time the grade was recorded.
assumptions: The timestamp is known to the source.

title: Feedback Sharing
description: The source element (P2) shares the feedback text with the destination (DS2). This act of sharing causes a threat because the recipient (DS2) can identify the specific feedback associated with the grade.
assumptions: The feedback text is known to the source.

title: Grade Record Sharing
description: The source element (P2) shares the entire grade record (student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, timestamp) with the destination (DS2). This act of sharing causes a threat because the recipient (DS2) can identify the specific grade record.
assumptions: The grade record is known to the source.

title: Data Processing
description: The destination element (DS2) receives the grade record and processes it. This act of processing causes a threat because the recipient (DS2) can identify the specific student, course, grader, and feedback associated with the grade.
assumptions: The recipient (DS2) has access to the data.

title: Data Storage
description: The destination element (DS2) stores the grade record. This act of storage causes a threat because the recipient (DS2) can identify the specific grade record and potentially use it for other purposes.
assumptions: The recipient (DS2) has access to the data.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The student (EE1) shares their personal identity information with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) to request grades and feedback.

title: Data Processing for Personalization
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the student's identity and uses it to personalize the feedback and grades, potentially linking the student to other data sources.

title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The portal shares the student's unique identifier (e.g., student ID or email) with the external entity (Student) without explicit consent or a clear, opt-in mechanism for the student to control this data sharing.

title: Teacher Feedback Disclosure
description: The portal shares the teacher's feedback (which may contain sensitive information about the student's academic performance or behavior) with the external entity (Student) without a privacy-preserving mechanism.

title: Data Processing for Identification
description: Upon receiving the student's grades and teacher feedback, the external entity (Student) processes this data to identify the student and potentially link it to other personal data (e.g., via a unique ID), which may be used for profiling or targeted advertising.

title: Identity Confusion
description: The parent entity (EE2) shares its identity with the child entity (EE1) without explicit authentication or authorization. This allows the child to potentially impersonate the parent or access data associated with the parent's identity.
assumptions: The parent account is linked to the child account, and the system does not enforce strict identity separation between them.

title: Data Processing Disclosure
description: The process (P1) processes the parent's identity information (EE2) and the child's identity information (EE1) to generate grades. This processing step may reveal sensitive identity data to unauthorized parties or for unintended purposes.
assumptions: The process does not have sufficient controls to mask or anonymize the identity data before processing.

title: Grade Data Exposure
description: The portal element (P1) shares the child's grade data with the parent (EE2) without any authentication or authorization checks. This allows the parent to access sensitive personal information.
assumptions: The portal is configured to display grades to any external entity.

title: Feedback Data Exposure
description: The portal element (P1) shares feedback data with the parent (EE2) without any authentication or authorization checks. This allows the parent to access sensitive personal information.
assumptions: The portal is configured to display feedback to any external entity.

title: Submission History Exposure
description: The portal element (P1) shares the child's submission history with the parent (EE2) without any authentication or authorization checks. This allows the parent to access sensitive personal information.
assumptions: The portal is configured to display submission history to any external entity.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The parent (EE2) receives the grades, feedback, and submission history and stores/processes them in a way that causes a privacy threat. The parent may use this data for its own purposes without the child's consent.
assumptions: The parent has no explicit consent to receive and process this specific data.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The external entity (EE4) shares personal identifiers (e.g., email, name) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) to create, modify, and disable accounts. This act of sharing causes the threat because the portal can now identify the user and potentially link their data to other entities.
assumptions: The external entity has the capability to share this metadata.

title: Data Linking via Meta-data
description: The data flow (DF12) transmits metadata about the parties involved (EE4 and P1) to the destination. This data-centric threat arises because the portal can use the sender's identity (EE4) to link or identify the recipient, potentially creating a profile or enabling targeted attacks.
assumptions: The data flow includes sender identity information.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The destination element (P1) receives the data and processes it in a way that causes a threat. The portal may store or use the parent-child relationship data (names, emails, roles) to create a persistent profile of the user, which could be used for surveillance or targeted access.
assumptions: The portal has the capability to store and process this data.

title: Data Leakage
description: The grading service (P2) writes account records and parent-child relationship links to the account directory (DS3). This action directly exposes sensitive personal data (account records, parent-child relationships) to unauthorized access or processing, constituting a data-centric threat where the act of sharing causes the threat.
assumptions: The service has the necessary permissions to write to DS3.

title: Data Processing Threat
description: The account directory (DS3) receives the account records and parent-child relationship links. Upon receipt, the system processes or stores this data in a way that causes a threat, such as making the data available for further processing, analytics, or potentially re-identification.
assumptions: The system at DS3 has the capability to process or store the incoming data in a manner that poses a privacy risk.

title: Data Leakage
description: The source element (Process P2) shares full grade records, assignments, and account directory with the external Cloud Hosting Provider (EE5) without any encryption or access controls. This act of sharing causes the threat of unauthorized data access.

title: Data in Transit
description: The data flow (DF14) transmits sensitive grade records, assignments, and account directory information over the network. This data-centric threat arises from the transmission of meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify the data recipients.

title: Unauthorized Processing
description: The destination element (Cloud Hosting Provider EE5) receives and processes the data in a way that causes the threat of storing or using the data for purposes not authorized by the data owner (P2).

title: Grade Records Access
description: The source element (DataStore DS2) shares grade records with the Assignment & Grading Service (Process P2). This act of sharing causes the threat because the destination element (P2) may process or store the data in a way that causes the threat.

title: Grade Records Processing
description: The destination element (Process P2) receives the grade records and processes them to build student, parent, and teacher views. This processing may cause the threat if the views are used to identify or link individuals inappropriately.
